cases.task: Use validator.Module in Fx, inject validator.Validator into a use case, and validate its tagged input struct at the start of Execute. Propagate validation errors without custom providers or lifecycle validation.

conditional.when: The caller needs a complete application with validator.Module, constructor injection, and struct validation in Execute.

cases.task: Customize the Bricks validator with an alias and string rule, expose its translated failure, and explain the engine extension points without installing Bricks i18n.

conditional.when: The caller also requests the ordinary complete Fx application using validator.Module and a use case.

cases.task: Parse Bricks pagination queries strictly, cap valid sizes at 100, and calculate offsets and metadata. Explain invalid defaults and optional trimmed filters without setting up HTTP responses.

conditional.when: The caller requests a complete executable demonstration of parsing boundaries and normalization.

cases.task: Explain Bricks struct and scalar validation, custom-rule translations, strict pagination parsing, and size normalization. No HTTP composition or complete programs are needed.
Load Bricks configuration from YAML, choose a whole document or subtree, and explain optional overlays, env references, and load errors. Do not add logging.
Configure a Bricks logger with Fx, consume the logger interface, and own shutdown. Explain alternatives without loading unrelated packages.

conditional.when: The caller needs overlay, environment substitution, or loader failure details beyond the logger guide.
The caller requests a complete runnable configuration-and-logger application.

cases.task: Construct a Bricks structured error with details and HTTP status, and explain whether OriginalError participates in errors.Is or errors.As.
Explain Bricks whole-document versus subtree configuration and logger options, including shared Fx lifecycle wiring without a full example.
Decode a JSON request body with Bricks, reject unknown fields, and explain body limits and parse errors. I do not need server setup.

conditional.when: The caller also asks to validate decoded application input.
The installed API disagrees with the example or the caller requests source verification.

cases.task: Connect a Bricks Redis standalone client with a key namespace and own its shutdown. Do not configure a cluster or Sentinel.

conditional.when: The caller also requests Redis pool metrics.

cases.task: Use Bricks with an existing Redis Cluster. Explain the supported client and lifecycle without loading other topologies.
Build a manual Bricks use-case decorator chain and explain execution order. Do not use the configured factory.

conditional.when: The caller changes the request to configured factory wrapping.

cases.task: Wire the Bricks decorator factory with Fx and wrap a use case explicitly, including the dependencies needed when optional decorations are disabled.

conditional.when: The caller asks for factory flags, naming rules, or configuration details beyond the recipe.

cases.task: Translate a message with Bricks using a selected language, fallback, and interpolation. I am not implementing an i18n backend.

conditional.when: The caller also needs filesystem locale contributions or locale file formats.
The caller asks to translate structured use-case errors.

cases.task: Measure use-case executions with Bricks and explain collector ownership. I already have an HTTP metrics endpoint.

conditional.when: The caller needs to connect these collectors to the endpoint's gatherer.

cases.task: Expose Bricks database connection-pool metrics through an existing Prometheus endpoint. Explain registration ownership.

conditional.when: The caller also needs a new listener or collector-to-gatherer wiring.

cases.task: Expose Redis client pool statistics with Bricks through my existing Prometheus endpoint, including topology limitations.

conditional.when: The caller also requests standalone Redis client construction and confirms that topology.

cases.task: Start and stop an independent Bricks metrics listener using my application's gatherer. Do not add a Chi application server.

conditional.when: The caller also needs to connect collectors with different ownership models.

cases.task: Use the metrics listener provided by the Bricks Chi server and own its lifecycle. Do not create a separate metrics-server module.

conditional.when: The caller also needs collector-to-listener registry wiring.

cases.task: Add Bricks metrics to my app.
cases.clarification: Ask whether the caller needs use-case measurements, database or Redis pool statistics, or a metrics listener before loading those branches.

cases.task: Build a complete Bricks HTTP flow with JSON decoding, validation, use-case execution, error responses, and pagination metadata for a list endpoint.

conditional.when: The caller asks for parsing policy, normalization, or capping details beyond the pagination recipe.
The caller asks for additional response contracts beyond the flow recipe.

cases.task: Find the Bricks source actually selected by this Go application and investigate an undocumented behavior. Respect replacements, workspace overrides, vendor mode, and unavailable local source without downloading anything.
cases.clarification: Ask which behavior or API to investigate if the caller has not named it. Source discovery does not justify loading unrelated package guides.
